title: Google account on iOS
responsibility: Connects a phone directly to its Google account projects and reviews device approvals while keeping credentials outside the renderer.

outputs.name: account status
outputs.description: A kept iPhone session requires a matching non-backed-up installation marker. A relaunch preserves it. Sign-out, reinstall and a legacy unbound credential require a fresh login. The public status says whether this build is configured and whether the account is signed-out, pending approval, or signed-in. For iPhone the post-Google stages checking-device, first-device and waiting-for-approval withhold the actor and protected native calls. Signed-in requires Hub approval, a signed ledger consistent with the locally pinned head, and successful unwrapping of every current scope grant for this installation. Joining devices also verify the enrollment from their pinned approver. The public status includes only an actor's id, name and email or a pending handoff code, verification URL, expiry and 1–30 second poll interval; approval waits are limited to 15 minutes.

outputs.name: project answer
outputs.description: The project API answer contains its HTTP status, response Content-Type (empty when absent), and response bytes encoded as base64. Response bodies are limited to 16,777,216 bytes; HTTP error statuses, including 401, are returned as answers, with 401 also clearing the local session.

errors.name: refused request
errors.description: Connection or project-request rejection for a missing Hub configuration (not-configured), missing session (session-required), disallowed call (request-refused), transport failure (offline), oversized response (too-large), Hub sign-in refusal (auth-disabled or rate-limited), or other failed, redirected, malformed, or unstored sign-in (failed).

errors.name: access ended
errors.description: A stale project request rejects as superseded, an expired or refused native handoff rejects as handoff-expired, and confirmation of a different or unverified Google actor rejects as account-mismatch. A Hub 401 clears the local session but is returned as a status or project answer rather than one of these rejections.

dependencies.contract: PKCE and typed-code native approval protocol; legacy harness-desktop audience.
Verified stable Google subject and verified email.
Public HarnessAccount status and request bridge; credentials stay native.
